short: A program that reads text and gives every possible next piece of text a probability.
One piece of text from a fixed list the model knows, often a whole word or part of one.
A number from 0 to 1 that says how likely something is. The probabilities of all options add up to 1.
The design behind most modern language models. It passes text through layers of attention and feed-forward steps.
The step where each token gathers information from itself and the tokens before it, taking more from the ones that match what it is looking for.
One of the numbers inside a model that is set during training. Our tiny model has about 1.3 million.
Adjusting a model's parameters, a little at a time, so its predictions on example text get better.
The fixed list of every token a model knows. Ours has 4,096 tokens, and GPT-2 has 50,257.
The number that stands for a token in the vocabulary. The model only ever sees these numbers.
A way to build a vocabulary. Start with single bytes, then keep joining the pair of pieces that appears together most often.
